sources_considered.why: Indeed Hiring Lab data on GenAI-related job postings, January 2023 to February 2024.
Bloomberg report giving OpenAI's headcount in April 2024: direct hiring by one generative AI firm.
HTTP 403; a secondary summary of the same Hiring Lab data.

receipt.public_excerpt: While still a very small share of total US jobs, GenAI-related jobs have grown rapidly since January 2023, from just 3 in 100,000 job postings to 11 in 10,000 as of the end of February 2024, a more than 30-fold increase.

evidence_items.explanation: GenAI-related postings grew fast but stayed at about 0.11% of US postings. That is real but small, and postings that mention GenAI are not shown to be net new jobs, so this neither clearly meets nor clearly fails a 'meaningful job creation' test.

receipt.public_excerpt: But today, both technologies are already creating new jobs, and have been for a while.

evidence_items.explanation: Indeed's economists say GenAI was already creating new jobs. This cuts against a literal reading of his words. They give no net or economy-wide count, so it does not settle the 'meaningful' reading.

receipt.public_excerpt: OpenAI now has about 1,200 employees, Lightcap said.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows direct hiring at a leading generative AI firm. This is gross hiring at one company and too small to count as economy-wide job creation under the plain reading.

unresolved_gaps: No source found that measures net new jobs caused by generative AI across the economy in 2023 to mid-2024.
His words give no threshold for 'meaningful', so a small but fast-growing pool of GenAI postings cannot be scored either way.
